questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: In Klein's SkillBuilder protocol for drawing valid Lewis structures of neutral organic molecules, what is the critical Step 1?

options.label: A
options.text: Count total valence electrons from all constituent atoms, add/subtract formal charges, and arrange the skeleton with the least electronegative atom (except H) central.

options.label: B
options.text: Connect all atoms in a single closed circle.

options.label: C
options.text: Draw double bonds to all hydrogen atoms.

options.label: D
options.text: Assign +1 charge to carbon and -1 to hydrogen.

questions.correct_answer: Count total valence electrons from all constituent atoms, add/subtract formal charges, and arrange the skeleton with the least electronegative atom (except H) central.
questions.explanation: Step 1 in Lewis structure assembly requires calculating the exact valence electron budget before distributing bonding and lone pairs.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: What severe chemical error is present when a student draws a neutral carbon atom with 5 single bonds (a 'Texas Carbon')?

options.label: A
options.text: Carbon has only 2 valence electrons.

options.label: B
options.text: Violation of the law of gravity.

options.label: C
options.text: Octet Rule violation: second-row carbon has only four valence orbitals (2s, 2px, 2py, 2pz) and cannot accommodate 10 valence electrons.

options.label: D
options.text: Hydrogen atoms cannot form single bonds.

questions.correct_answer: Octet Rule violation: second-row carbon has only four valence orbitals (2s, 2px, 2py, 2pz) and cannot accommodate 10 valence electrons.
questions.explanation: Carbon cannot expand its valence octet; drawing 5 bonds (10 electrons) is a fundamental octet violation.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.topic: SkillBuilder: Curved Arrow Electron Flow Rules
questions.question: When debugging a proposed mechanism step, which curved arrow error violates the Law of Conservation of Charge?

options.label: A
options.text: Drawing an arrow from a nucleophile to an electrophilic carbonyl.

options.label: B
options.text: Drawing an arrow from a pi bond to a carbocation.

options.label: C
options.text: Drawing an arrow from a lone pair to a proton.

options.label: D
options.text: Drawing an arrow originating from a positive charge to a neutral atom, creating a net change in overall formal charge across the elementary step.

questions.correct_answer: Drawing an arrow originating from a positive charge to a neutral atom, creating a net change in overall formal charge across the elementary step.
questions.explanation: Curved arrows represent electron flow (negative charge motion); arrows must originate at electron-rich pairs/bonds, never at formal positive charges.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: Which curved arrow maneuver is STRICTLY FORBIDDEN when drawing resonance contributors of a conjugated molecule?

options.label: A
options.text: Polarizing a carbonyl pi bond toward oxygen.

options.label: B
options.text: Moving a lone pair into an adjacent pi bond.

options.label: C
options.text: Breaking single (sigma) bonds or altering the underlying atomic connectivity of the molecular framework.

options.label: D
options.text: Delocalizing pi electrons into an adjacent vacant p orbital.

questions.correct_answer: Breaking single (sigma) bonds or altering the underlying atomic connectivity of the molecular framework.
questions.explanation: Resonance structures differ ONLY in the placement of pi electrons and nonbonding lone pairs; sigma bond frameworks must remain identical.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: Using Klein's 4-step ARIO SkillBuilder decision tree, how do you determine which side of an acid-base equilibrium is favored?

options.label: A
options.text: Identify conjugate bases, compare relative stability using Atom → Resonance → Induction → Orbital (ARIO), and shift equilibrium toward the WEAKER acid (higher pKa).

options.label: B
options.text: Equilibrium always favors the molecule with more carbon atoms.

options.label: C
options.text: Equilibrium always favors the stronger acid.

options.label: D
options.text: Equilibrium is always exactly 50:50.

questions.correct_answer: Identify conjugate bases, compare relative stability using Atom → Resonance → Induction → Orbital (ARIO), and shift equilibrium toward the WEAKER acid (higher pKa).
questions.explanation: The side containing the more stable conjugate base (derived from the weaker acid with higher pKa) is thermodynamically favored.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: In Klein's SkillBuilder algorithm for naming polyfunctional alkanes, what is the first priority step?

options.label: A
options.text: Number from right to left alphabetically.

options.label: B
options.text: Identify the longest continuous carbon chain containing the principal functional group, and number from the end providing the lowest locant number at the first point of difference.

options.label: C
options.text: Ignore all branching substituents.

options.label: D
options.text: Name all substituents in random order.

questions.correct_answer: Identify the longest continuous carbon chain containing the principal functional group, and number from the end providing the lowest locant number at the first point of difference.
questions.explanation: IUPAC rules require finding the principal parent carbon chain and numbering to give substituents the lowest possible locants at the first point of difference.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: In Klein's SkillBuilder for analyzing butane Newman projections along the C2-C3 bond, which conformation represents the absolute energy minimum?

options.label: A
options.text: The fully eclipsed conformation (0° dihedral angle, methyls overlapping).

options.label: B
options.text: The gauche conformation (60° dihedral angle).

options.label: C
options.text: The anti-periplanar conformation (dihedral angle 180° between methyl groups, minimizing torsional and steric strain).

options.label: D
options.text: The eclipsed conformation (0° dihedral angle).

questions.correct_answer: The anti-periplanar conformation (dihedral angle 180° between methyl groups, minimizing torsional and steric strain).
questions.explanation: The anti conformation places bulky methyl groups as far apart as possible (180°), eliminating steric and torsional strain.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: In the 3-step SkillBuilder for assigning (R)/(S) configuration at a stereocenter, what do you do if two attached atoms have identical atomic numbers?

options.label: A
options.text: Ignore both groups.

options.label: B
options.text: Flip a coin to decide priority.

options.label: C
options.text: Compare the list of attached atoms in descending atomic number order at the next point of difference along the substituent paths until a tie is broken.

options.label: D
options.text: Assign priority based on the total number of hydrogen atoms.

questions.correct_answer: Compare the list of attached atoms in descending atomic number order at the next point of difference along the substituent paths until a tie is broken.
questions.explanation: When immediate atoms tie, compare the highest-atomic-number attached atoms at subsequent coordination spheres until priority is resolved.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.topic: SkillBuilder: Chair Conformation Flip and Stability
questions.question: In Klein's SkillBuilder for substituted cyclohexanes, how do axial and equatorial substituents change upon a chair flip?

options.label: A
options.text: The ring converts into a flat planar hexagon.

options.label: B
options.text: Substituents detach and swap positions randomly.

options.label: C
options.text: All 'up' groups become 'down'.

options.label: D
options.text: All axial groups become equatorial, and all equatorial groups become axial, while retaining their 'up' or 'down' relative stereochemical orientation.

questions.correct_answer: All axial groups become equatorial, and all equatorial groups become axial, while retaining their 'up' or 'down' relative stereochemical orientation.
questions.explanation: A chair flip interconverts axial/equatorial positions, but preserves the configurational up/down relationships of all ring substituents.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: Why does a proposed Grignard reaction (CH₃MgBr + 4-hydroxycyclohexanone) fail to produce the desired tertiary alcohol?

options.label: A
options.text: Proton quenching roadblock: the strongly basic Grignard reagent (pKa ~ 50) is instantly destroyed by acid-base reaction with the acidic hydroxyl group (pKa ~ 16) before attacking the ketone.

options.label: B
options.text: Because cyclohexanone cannot form tertiary alcohols.

options.label: C
options.text: Because Grignard reagents only react with esters.

options.label: D
options.text: Because the reaction explodes at -78°C.

questions.correct_answer: Proton quenching roadblock: the strongly basic Grignard reagent (pKa ~ 50) is instantly destroyed by acid-base reaction with the acidic hydroxyl group (pKa ~ 16) before attacking the ketone.
questions.explanation: Grignard reagents are strong bases; any acidic proton (alcohol, amine, alkyne, water) will destroy the reagent before nucleophilic addition can occur.

options.label: C
options.text: Moving a lone pair into an adjacent pi bond.

options.label: D
options.text: Delocalizing pi electrons into an adjacent vacant p orbital.

questions.correct_answer: Breaking single (sigma) bonds or altering the underlying atomic connectivity of the molecular framework.
questions.explanation: Resonance structures differ ONLY in the placement of pi electrons and nonbonding lone pairs; sigma bond frameworks must remain identical.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: Using Klein's 4-step ARIO SkillBuilder decision tree, how do you determine which side of an acid-base equilibrium is favored?

options.label: A
options.text: Equilibrium always favors the stronger acid.

options.label: B
options.text: Equilibrium always favors the molecule with more carbon atoms.

options.label: C
options.text: Identify conjugate bases, compare relative stability using Atom → Resonance → Induction → Orbital (ARIO), and shift equilibrium toward the WEAKER acid (higher pKa).

options.label: D
options.text: Equilibrium is always exactly 50:50.

questions.correct_answer: Identify conjugate bases, compare relative stability using Atom → Resonance → Induction → Orbital (ARIO), and shift equilibrium toward the WEAKER acid (higher pKa).
questions.explanation: The side containing the more stable conjugate base (derived from the weaker acid with higher pKa) is thermodynamically favored.

questions.question: In Klein's SkillBuilder algorithm for naming polyfunctional alkanes, what is the first priority step?

options.label: C
options.text: Number from right to left alphabetically.

options.label: D
options.text: Identify the longest continuous carbon chain containing the principal functional group, and number from the end providing the lowest locant number at the first point of difference.

questions.correct_answer: Identify the longest continuous carbon chain containing the principal functional group, and number from the end providing the lowest locant number at the first point of difference.
questions.explanation: IUPAC rules require finding the principal parent carbon chain and numbering to give substituents the lowest possible locants at the first point of difference.

questions.question: In Klein's SkillBuilder for analyzing butane Newman projections along the C2-C3 bond, which conformation represents the absolute energy minimum?

options.label: C

questions.explanation: The anti conformation places bulky methyl groups as far apart as possible (180°), eliminating steric and torsional strain.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: In the 3-step SkillBuilder for assigning (R)/(S) configuration at a stereocenter, what do you do if two attached atoms have identical atomic numbers?

options.label: A
options.text: Assign priority based on the total number of hydrogen atoms.

options.label: B
options.text: Compare the list of attached atoms in descending atomic number order at the next point of difference along the substituent paths until a tie is broken.

options.label: C
options.text: Ignore both groups.

options.label: D
options.text: Flip a coin to decide priority.

questions.correct_answer: Compare the list of attached atoms in descending atomic number order at the next point of difference along the substituent paths until a tie is broken.
questions.explanation: When immediate atoms tie, compare the highest-atomic-number attached atoms at subsequent coordination spheres until priority is resolved.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.topic: SkillBuilder: Chair Conformation Flip and Stability
questions.question: In Klein's SkillBuilder for substituted cyclohexanes, how do axial and equatorial substituents change upon a chair flip?

options.label: A
options.text: All axial groups become equatorial, and all equatorial groups become axial, while retaining their 'up' or 'down' relative stereochemical orientation.

options.label: B
options.text: The ring converts into a flat planar hexagon.

options.label: C
options.text: Substituents detach and swap positions randomly.

options.label: D
options.text: All 'up' groups become 'down'.

questions.correct_answer: All axial groups become equatorial, and all equatorial groups become axial, while retaining their 'up' or 'down' relative stereochemical orientation.
questions.explanation: A chair flip interconverts axial/equatorial positions, but preserves the configurational up/down relationships of all ring substituents.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: Why does a proposed Grignard reaction (CH₃MgBr + 4-hydroxycyclohexanone) fail to produce the desired tertiary alcohol?

options.label: A
options.text: Because cyclohexanone cannot form tertiary alcohols.

options.label: B
options.text: Because Grignard reagents only react with esters.

options.label: C
options.text: Because the reaction explodes at -78°C.

options.label: D
options.text: Proton quenching roadblock: the strongly basic Grignard reagent (pKa ~ 50) is instantly destroyed by acid-base reaction with the acidic hydroxyl group (pKa ~ 16) before attacking the ketone.

questions.correct_answer: Proton quenching roadblock: the strongly basic Grignard reagent (pKa ~ 50) is instantly destroyed by acid-base reaction with the acidic hydroxyl group (pKa ~ 16) before attacking the ketone.
questions.explanation: Grignard reagents are strong bases; any acidic proton (alcohol, amine, alkyne, water) will destroy the reagent before nucleophilic addition can occur.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: In Klein's SkillBuilder protocol for drawing valid Lewis structures of neutral organic molecules, what is the critical Step 1?

options.label: A
options.text: Assign +1 charge to carbon and -1 to hydrogen.

options.label: B
options.text: Connect all atoms in a single closed circle.

options.label: C
options.text: Count total valence electrons from all constituent atoms, add/subtract formal charges, and arrange the skeleton with the least electronegative atom (except H) central.

options.label: D
options.text: Draw double bonds to all hydrogen atoms.

questions.correct_answer: Count total valence electrons from all constituent atoms, add/subtract formal charges, and arrange the skeleton with the least electronegative atom (except H) central.
questions.explanation: Step 1 in Lewis structure assembly requires calculating the exact valence electron budget before distributing bonding and lone pairs.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: What severe chemical error is present when a student draws a neutral carbon atom with 5 single bonds (a 'Texas Carbon')?

options.label: A
options.text: Carbon has only 2 valence electrons.

options.label: B
options.text: Octet Rule violation: second-row carbon has only four valence orbitals (2s, 2px, 2py, 2pz) and cannot accommodate 10 valence electrons.

options.label: C
options.text: Hydrogen atoms cannot form single bonds.

options.label: D
options.text: Violation of the law of gravity.

questions.correct_answer: Octet Rule violation: second-row carbon has only four valence orbitals (2s, 2px, 2py, 2pz) and cannot accommodate 10 valence electrons.
questions.explanation: Carbon cannot expand its valence octet; drawing 5 bonds (10 electrons) is a fundamental octet violation.

options.text: Drawing an arrow from a pi bond to a carbocation.

options.label: B
options.text: Drawing an arrow from a nucleophile to an electrophilic carbonyl.

options.label: C
options.text: Drawing an arrow from a lone pair to a proton.

options.label: D
options.text: Drawing an arrow originating from a positive charge to a neutral atom, creating a net change in overall formal charge across the elementary step.

questions.correct_answer: Drawing an arrow originating from a positive charge to a neutral atom, creating a net change in overall formal charge across the elementary step.
questions.explanation: Curved arrows represent electron flow (negative charge motion); arrows must originate at electron-rich pairs/bonds, never at formal positive charges.
